newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares firm, seen tracking sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares firm, seen tracking sideways.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index rebounded on Thursday after a decline of 2.4 percent in the previous two days and traders forecast the index would be relatively stable over the forthcoming week.

"Heavy selling is not likely because the general feeling is that September will give a new push to prices as foreign and domestic demand is expected to increase significantly then once the summer holidays are over," an analyst said.
The SBI index climbed 10.5 points or 0.69 percent to 1,554.17. Overall 13 shares rose, five fell, one was unchanged and nine were untraded. Turnover fell to 125.7 million tolars from 203.9 million.
Drug company Lek was the most actively traded stock, up 1.4 percent to 35,490 tolars on volume of 1,691 shares for total turnover of 60 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Dadas was the biggest gainer, rising 9.46 percent to 5,900 tolars on volume of 40 shares in a rebound after a fall of 10.17 percent on Wednesday.
Financial consultancy Finmedia led the decliners, closing 5.45 percent lower at 10,400 on volume of 26 shares.

Pharmaceutical firm Krka, which is listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) market and today announced a 14 percent increase in first half net profit, remained unchanged at 25,000 tolars on volume of 4,167 shares.
In terms of long-term investments, one analyst rated food company Droga, chemical firm Pinus, bank Probanka and trader Mercator as attractive options based on their share price and expected results.
